description: Build a CSV of corrected titles and image alt text from a catalog, for the user to review and import. Use it for "write the alt text for my images", "fix the shouting titles". Pass csv or domain, not both; optional fixes (alt_text, title_whitespace, title_caps) and alt_text_template with {title}, {vendor}, {type}, {position}. Returns csv with only the rows that change (URL handle, Title, Product image URL, Image position, Image alt text), up to 200 rows, and counts. Advisory: nothing is changed in any store. Nothing is stored: the file or feed is used for this answer and dropped.

alt_text_template.description: Alt text pattern with {title}, {vendor}, {type} and {position} placeholders (default "{title}")

csv.description: The product CSV text exactly as exported from Shopify, header row included. At most 2 MB.

domain.description: A store address such as example.com, instead of csv. The store's public /products.json is read once (at most 5 pages of 250 products), after its robots.txt. Large stores often block it.

fixes.description: alt_text: fill empty image alt text from the template. title_whitespace: trim and collapse spaces in titles. title_caps: rewrite all-capital titles in title case. Default: all three.

name: listing_fix_sheet

csv.description: Rows to import: URL handle, Title, Product image URL, Image position, Image alt text. Only rows that change are included.

feed_truncated.description: True when the store has more products than the five pages read

host.description: The store read, in domain mode

totals.description: Fixes found before the sheet was cut to 200 rows

title: Build a CSV of listing text fixes
